summary: Skookum Peak, Pend Oreille County WA: a 1937 10-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab, abandoned in the 1950s; gone, with footings and bed frames photographed on site.

facts.design: 10-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Listed as gone (firelookout.com) and removed (Washington lookouts index); WillhiteWeb photos, undated on the page, show footings, bed frames and a flagpole or telephone pole still standing

access.note: The mountain is public land, but the road from Bead Lake Road crosses private parcels and is blocked by a gate and trespass signs. WillhiteWeb withheld the route to avoid trouble with neighbors

visit.trail_note: No route published. Approaches cross private land and the Bead Lake Road route is gated and posted

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says gone and the Washington lookouts index says removed. Both agree that no tower stands, so the story reports both words as the sources give them.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: only the 1937 build year is dated; the 1950s abandonment is a decade only, so no event year is logged for it. WillhiteWeb photos carry no date on the page, so the on-site remains may be old. Access is 'restricted' because the approach crosses private land behind a gate and trespass signs; the story gives no route and advises staying off posted land. Facts.height_m 3.0 converts the FFLOS '10 foot pole tower' and may describe pole length rather than tower height. Two web searches found no other history for this site.
